rationale: PHP 7.0 made `self` and `parent` SEMI-RESERVED: they may not name a top-level declaration, but they MAY name a method, a property or a class constant, because a member is reached through its owner and cannot be confused with the type position the keyword occupies. The production symbol filter refuses php symbols BY NAME (`src/ast/pool-worker.ts` keepSymbol, `RESERVED = { php: new Set(["self", "parent"]) }`) with no reference to kind or owner, so it deletes legal members while the analyzer still emits the `contains` edges that name them — an edge whose endpoint is not in the store. Measured over the whole admitted population (5,094 files, 350,342 edges): exactly ONE such edge exists, `contains Node -> parent` at `phpmyadmin/src/Navigation/Nodes/Node.php:54` (`public Node|null $parent = null;`), and it is the only edge in the lane naming a declaration the store does not hold. Authored and RUN BEFORE the fix: on the unfixed tree this file publishes 3 symbols (namespace, class, `probe`) and 0 of the 5 member declarations below, while emitting 2 `contains Holder -> parent` rows and 3 `contains Holder -> self` rows — the defect at fixture scale. The half of the rule that must SURVIVE (a php class/interface/trait/enum/namespace/top-level function named `parent`/`self`) cannot be written as valid php — `class parent {}` is a parse error — so it is pinned by the injectable mutant `php/drop-keyword-named-members`, which re-instates the name-only drop at the result level; these `expectSymbols` rows are what catch it. The owner rows are the resolution contract the receiver-owner round established: a member edge must carry `metadata.owner`, because the bare name `parent` is a keyword and a member name at once and only `(ownerName, name)` distinguishes the two.

expectSymbols.name: parent
expectSymbols.comment: THE FIX, property form: `public ?Holder $parent = null;` is legal php and must publish.

expectSymbols.name: parent
expectSymbols.comment: constant form: `public const parent = 'P';` — semi-reserved words are legal class-constant names (this file parses with 0 error nodes, probed against the pinned wasm).

expectSymbols.name: self
expectSymbols.comment: method form: `public function self(): string` — the form PHP's own documentation uses to illustrate semi-reserved names.

expectSymbols.name: probe
expectSymbols.comment: the caller, published before and after; present so the file's fixture ids stay stable

expectRelationships.comment: THE DANGLING EDGE, now resolvable: the analyzer has always emitted this containment (twice, at the property and the constant), which is why a deleted symbol left an edge naming nothing.
same shape, three times over (property, constant, method)

`$this->parent` (property read) and `self::parent` (constant fetch) both target `parent` with the owner carried, so the (owner, name) key resolves to exactly one declaration instead of colliding with every other class that has a `parent`.
`$this->self()` — the call itself, labelled `calls`, distinct from the property read of the same name

forbidSymbols.name: parent
forbidSymbols.comment: THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX, and the half that cannot be written as valid php: `class parent {}` is a parse error, so no fixture FILE can declare one and only an injectable mutant can produce it. A symbol named `parent` with NO owner must not be published, because the exemption the fix grants is exactly `(member kind, owner present)` — and a bare `parent` in the store is a resolution candidate for every `parent::` / `$this->parent` edge at once. Caught by `php/publish-ownerless-reserved-names`. `ownerName: null` is the top-level absent-or-null convention (`script/m14/run-fixtures.ts:375`), not an ignored field: this row must FAIL for an ownerless `parent` and PASS for the `Holder`-owned property and constant that expectSymbols above requires.

forbidSymbols.name: self
forbidSymbols.comment: same for `self` — the top-level-declaration form of the semi-reserved rule.

forbidRelationships.comment: a member read of a keyword-named member with NO owner is the shape that makes `parent` ambiguous between the keyword and every class's `parent` member; the owner is what the resolution contract rests on
